title: 3+-way ECMP (N>=3) is untested — only the 2-way diamond is covered
evidence: core/ecmp_test.odin:75 testing.expectf(t, count == 2, "diamond source has 2 equal-cost next hops, got %d", count); :122 testing.expectf(t, ecmp_pick(7, 9, 0, 42, 2) < 2, "ecmp_pick n=2 in range [0,2)"); :131 bucket := [2]int{}; :133 bucket[int(ecmp_pick(0, 3, 0, pkt_id, 2))] += 1
detail: Every ECMP test uses a 2-way diamond; ecmp_pick is never called with n>=3 and no 3+-way junction is built. Only n=1 and n=2 exercise the % n branch and multi-hop array packing.
recommended_fix: Add a test with three equal-cost middle routers (count==3): assert all 3 hops pack into hops[] and ecmp_pick distributes across all 3 buckets.

title: next_packet_id determinism has no direct assertion — relied on transitively by affinity + replay
evidence: core/ecmp_test.odin:207 // run B: fresh run, same seed + same log + same demand; the SAME packet id; :208 // (next_packet_id is deterministic) -> the SAME first hop. Grep of core/*_test.odin for direct packet-id equality asserts (.id ==, packets[0].id, next_packet_id ==) returns none.
detail: Flow affinity across two runs presumes identical packet ids, but no expect asserts it. Covered only transitively — a packet-id regression would surface as an affinity/replay failure, not a localized one.
recommended_fix: Add an explicit expect that two same-seed runs assign identical ids, e.g. testing.expect(t, a.flow.packets[0].id == b.flow.packets[0].id), to localize the failure.
